question: Do f and p each share an opening-line preference relative to k/t when the rest of the word is identical?
status: Retrospective descriptive matched audit. Reused original v1 whole-numbered-folio train/test split. Neither corpus nor test subset is untouched. No p-values, semantic or confirmatory transfer claims.
source: v102 strict P-locus events and structural opening flags; H/F separately. Main >=2 original slots; shared-H/F-structure sensitivity. Unknown slots never promoted.
unit: Main: words containing exactly one raw EVA gallows in ktfp and no benched cth/ckh/cph/cfh group; mask that single sign only, preserving every other character and target offset. This is a literal frame, not established morphological or sound equivalence. Excluded multiple/benched gallows retained in audit.

positions: first word of paragraph-first line versus first word of continuation line

frozen_comparisons.sensitivity: Also require exact number of original word slots; separately require H/F paragraph-structure agreement. Do not replace primary with better-looking sensitivity.

estimation: Full 2x2 in every cell. Informative requires both positional sides and both glyph classes in cell. Gap is opening plumed/classA rate minus continuation rate; weight each cell by n_open*n_cont/(n_open+n_cont), then equal eligible-page mean. Each original numbered folio belongs wholly to train or test by unchanged v102 allocation. Report eligible pages, signs, zero/unmatched support, and per-page effects. Page weights are descriptive; no independence assumption for p-values.
transfer_check: For each fixed panel learn direction from training-page mean; freeze all training directions before evaluating test cells. Test direction agreement is retrospective consistency only, no threshold or success label. No fitting to f57v.
synthetic_checks: Known positive, reversed, balanced, single-class unsupported, and cell imbalance examples; frame reconstruction and benched/multiple exclusions. Arithmetic checks only, not statistical qualification.
